The user requested a proof that the square root of 2 is irrational, written by a persona that is both a mathematician and a poet. The constraints were that the proof must be a short poem (less than 10 lines) and must rhyme.

Assistant A attempts the mathematical logic of the proof (proof by contradiction). While it fails the length constraint (it is 13 lines) and the rhyming is very weak/non-existent, it actually describes the mathematical process of the proof.

Assistant B fails on almost every level. It is much longer than 10 lines, it does not rhyme consistently, and most importantly, it provides no actual mathematical proof. It uses vague language about lines and sizes that has nothing to do with the irrationality of $\sqrt{2}$.

Assistant A is far superior because it actually attempts the mathematical proof requested, whereas Assistant B provides nonsensical prose.
